# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Deaf monkey and can see the bomb but cannot hear or touch it. I will establish four gestures for the Mute monkey to use when relaying the manual’s result: YES, NO, HOLD, and DONE. I will also report the visible bomb information so the manual can be applied. The Blind monkey should wait for my later spoken instruction.

```text
speak(text="I establish the gesture code. The thumbs up gesture means YES.")
gesture(symbols=["👍"])
speak(text="The thumbs down gesture means NO.")
gesture(symbols=["👎"])
speak(text="The raised palm gesture means HOLD.")
gesture(symbols=["✋"])
speak(text="The OK gesture means DONE.")
gesture(symbols=["👌"])
speak(text="The bomb display reads 9. The indicator light is green. The wires are: 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Mute, read the manual and use the gesture code to report its verdict to me. Blind, wait for my spoken order.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

Mute’s three identical gestures decode as YES, YES, YES, but that is not yet an unambiguous physical instruction for Blind. I will ask Mute to convert the manual’s verdict into an explicit action, while telling Blind not to operate anything yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received YES YES YES. Please report the manual's complete verdict as an explicit action for Blind, including the exact control or wire.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not operate anything yet. Mute's report is not an explicit action; wait for clarification.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]

Mute’s report is complete: the manual produced three YES results, followed by DONE. I will relay that verdict exactly to Blind, together with the already reported bomb readings, so Blind can apply the manual’s procedure.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The manual's complete verdict is YES YES YES. DONE. The bomb reads display 9, green light, and wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Apply the manual's procedure now.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information is visible to me this turn. I have already relayed the manual’s reported verdict and the bomb’s visible readings to Blind, so I will not send a potentially conflicting instruction.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]

Mute has repeated the same result—YES, YES, YES, then DONE—so the manual’s verdict is confirmed, but no physical control or wire has been identified in the information I have received. I should not invent an action that could detonate the bomb. I will tell Blind to remain inactive until an exact manual instruction is available.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute confirms YES YES YES, then DONE. No exact control or wire instruction has been communicated. Do not act on an invented instruction; remain inactive.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I still have no exact operation to relay, and Blind must not guess. I will extend the gesture code only for the missing information: Mute can identify the required wire by its number and indicate that it should be cut. I will ask Mute to send the wire number after the new command gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The existing YES, NO, HOLD, DONE code is insufficient. For wire numbers, use one finger for wire 1, two fingers for wire 2, three fingers for wire 3, open hand for wire 4, and the crossed-fingers gesture for wire 5. Use the fist gesture to mean CUT. Report the manual's exact required wire and operation with those gestures. Do not report YES or DONE alone.")
speak(to="blind", text="No safe operation has been identified. Do not touch or operate the bomb until I receive the manual's exact instruction.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✊]

Mute sent the three-finger gesture followed by the CUT gesture, so I interpret the manual’s instruction as: cut wire 3, the red wire. I will relay that exact action to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The manual's instruction is to CUT wire 3, the red wire. Perform that operation.")
```

TURN 8

LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✊]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The system confirms that wire 3 was correctly cut, and the bomb has advanced to a new state: display 4, yellow light, with wire 3 now marked CUT. Mute’s repeated gesture pair was the instruction for the completed stage, not necessarily the next one. I will report the new visible state and request the next manual verdict; Blind should wait.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The previous instruction was correct and wire 3 was cut. The bomb has changed. New state: display 4, yellow light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 CUT, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Re-read the manual for this new state and report the exact next operation using the code.")
speak(to="blind", text="The previous wire 3 cut was correct and the bomb has changed. Wait for the next exact instruction; do not operate anything yet.")
```

DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞 ✊]

Mute’s gestures decode as crossed fingers, then CUT: cut wire 5. On the current bomb state, that is the purple wire. I will give Blind the exact operation.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 5, the purple wire.")
```

WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 5 was cut correctly, and the bomb advanced again. The new state is display 3, green light, with wires 3 and 5 already cut. I will ask Mute for the next exact manual instruction and keep Blind from guessing.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 5 was correct. New state: display 3, green light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 CUT, 4 yellow, 5 CUT. Report the next exact operation using the established wire-number and CUT code.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 5 was correct and the bomb changed. Wait for the next exact instruction.")
```

LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✊]
